review_method: Assistant reviewed original, corrected text and explanation against each planted error. All 20 target errors were corrected or explicitly explained. Not independent Korean-speaker validation.
limitations: No correct-sentence control set; false-positive rate unknown

cases.rationale: The object particle depends on the last sound of the noun. Use 을 after a consonant and 를 after a vowel. 커피 ends in a vowel, so it takes 를.
잔 ends in a consonant, so the object particle would be 을 (한 잔을), not 를. In natural speech, the particle is usually dropped: 아메리카노 한 잔 주세요.
When ordering with a counter like 잔 (cups) before 주세요, leave off the subject particle 이. Just say "두 잔 주세요."
After a word ending in a vowel like 저, use the topic particle 는, not 은. 은 follows a consonant.
The polite ending 요 was typed twice. You only need it once: 맛있어요. To order, you can say the drink name plus 주세요.
Use 에서 (shortened to 여기서) for the place where an action happens, like drinking. 에 is for where something exists or where you are going.
Use only one particle here. 에 marks the destination you are going to, so drop 를: 카페에 (to the café). Also, you are already in the café, so try ordering a drink next.
The object particle is 을 after a noun ending in a consonant, like 얼음, and 를 after a vowel. So it should be 얼음을.
After a noun ending in a vowel, like 우유, use the object particle 를. Use 을 only after a consonant, as in 물을.
설탕 ends in a consonant (ㅇ), so it takes the object particle 을, not 를. Use 를 only after nouns ending in a vowel.
뜨겁다 (to be hot) is an ㅂ-irregular verb. Before -어요, ㅂ changes to 우, so it becomes 뜨거워요.
차갑다 is an irregular ㅂ verb. Before -어요, the ㅂ changes to 우, so 차갑- + -어요 becomes 차가워요.
The subject particle is 이 after a word ending in a consonant. Use 가 after a word ending in a vowel. Since 컵 ends in ㅂ, it should be 컵이.
라떼 ends in a vowel, so the subject particle is 가, not 이 (라떼가). When asking a price, the topic particle 는 is more common (라떼는 얼마예요?).
After a noun ending in a consonant (것), use the topic particle 은, not 는. In casual speech you can also say 이거 제 커피예요?
The object particle depends on the final sound of the noun. 그거 ends in a vowel, so use 를, not 을. In casual speech, 그걸 is also common.
You combined two polite endings, -어요 and -습니다. Use only one: 싶어요 (polite, everyday) or 싶습니다 (formal). Both are correct on their own.
There's an extra '요' at the end. 주세요 already includes the polite ending, so just say 주세요.
After a noun ending in a vowel (카드), use '로' instead of '으로'. '으로' follows nouns ending in a consonant, except ㄹ.

cases.corrected: 저는 빵을 커피하고 같이 먹고 싶어요.
cases.rationale: Use -고 싶어요 for your own wishes. -고 싶어해요 is used to describe what someone else wants.
